contracts: (A negative Probe is successful only when the process failure proves the declared defect with its declared diagnostic category; wrong or absent diagnostics are rejected, and infrastructure failures terminate distinctly without satisfying the negative-Probe validation result.) AND (A successful Replay Result contains independently verified non-authority bindings and authorizes=[]; missing, copied, self-reported, or mismatched bindings are rejected.) AND (Fresh replay reports Exact Cover equality and no unexplained orphan nodes; otherwise reproduction is rejected.) AND (Pass iff every applicable Consumer receipt binds the current approved Candidate Route, real invocation, actual interface, input, command, output, result, and dependencies, with the current result captured from that invocation; otherwise fail with no successful re-enable verdict.) AND (Support policy is independently verified; omitted or solely inferred verification is unsuccessful.) AND (Terminal reproduction succeeds only when reconstructed identity matches the original and fresh replay verdict equals the pinned verdict; otherwise it fails closed.) AND (The S7 selector passes on Windows while its assertions reject user-profile paths as current authority.) AND (The isolated root-escape invocation fails before validator execution and produces neither a successful validation receipt nor a trusted replay result.) AND (The planned selector accepts a verdict only when it links to current source identity and real execution, and rejects either missing linkage.) AND (The replay validator reconstructs the original binding identity, replays through the original wrapper with that same identity, and rejects no-launch or identity-mismatch claims.) AND (The rollback selector records baseline observation for 100% of non-empty Consumer Manifest entries across every applicable route transition.) AND (The selector first reconstructs the literal original binding identity, uses that same identity for replay, and rejects any identity mismatch.) AND (The selector observes a deterministic rejected or blocked outcome and no unsupported or substituted target is accepted.) AND (The targeted test observes non-zero termination, a missing-validator-capability diagnostic, no substituted validator identity, and no Replay Result artifact.) AND (The terminal result rejects the illegal target and records no accepted or substituted effective target.)

Each declared assertion needs a cer_assertion mapping and a meaningful independent oracle. Tests must invoke the real production entry. The plan is not a behavior observation. Keep governance/constraint failures non-authorizing; do not emit expected-red for them. Preserve all bound Given/When/Then and forbidden outcomes. No placeholder pass or synthetic RED.

selector_intents: Cause timeout, import/dependency failure, non-start, or failure before validation in the detached process; verify separate infrastructure/execution classification rather than declared validation failure.
Check the run output after rejection; fail if any Replay Result artifact is created for the missing-capability invocation.
Configure the missing-capability case so any fallback or substituted validator is observable; fail if a different validator is selected or validation proceeds.
Execute a detached negative Probe that succeeds or whose failure lacks the declared defect evidence; verify that a nonzero result alone is not accepted.
Execute a detached negative Probe whose declared defect produces a diagnostic category different from its declared expected category; verify rejection as a diagnostic mismatch.
Execute replay with a missing, copied, or self-reported non-authority binding and observe rejection of the successful-result path.
Execute the historical replay selector with replay inputs whose identity differs from the reconstructed original binding identity and observe rejection.
Execute the isolated root-escape capability case through validate-package; fail the test unless capability resolution rejects before validator execution and no trusted result is emitted.
Execute the replay selector with an unsupported target and require the red rejection outcome.
Execute the rollback selector for a non-empty Consumer Manifest entry whose post-rollback observation differs from the Prior Behavior Baseline and observe failure.
Exercise support-policy verification with the independent verification absent or replaced by a dependent result and require the selector to fail.

Exercise the bound Given/When against the real production entry. Only a failing assertion of the unchanged observable and expected outcome may emit this marker. Expected subject rejection is a passing test when the oracle requires rejection. Import, setup, process launch, timeout and infrastructure faults must never emit this marker. Observable: The S7 pytest result contains assertions for Windows execution and authority-safe path handling. Expected: The authored S7 test executes replay assertions on Windows, confirms declared platform support, and rejects a user-profile path as current authority.
Invoke the replay/validation entry point with the required validator capability absent; expect deterministic unsuccessful termination and no Replay Result.
Reconstruct the original binding identity, run fresh replay with that identity, and fail when the terminal semantic verdict differs or equality is asserted without machine evidence.
Run the fresh-replay Exact Cover selector with a pinned-graph mismatch or orphan-node mutation and observe rejection.
Run the historical-wrapper no-launch fault witness through the replay validator.
Run the planned replay verdict selector with real-execution trace omitted and observe executable verdict validation fail.
Run the planned replay verdict selector with source-identity linkage omitted and observe executable verdict validation fail.
Run the target-validation selector against an illegal target and require its rejection as the observed RED result.
The S7 test rejects Windows handling that treats a user-profile path as current authority or cannot execute the supported replay path.
scripts/sc/tests/tc_d1_cer/test_s7.py::test_reenable_rejects_stale_or_unapproved_candidate_route supplies a stale or unapproved Candidate Route identity; the validator must reject the receipt.

scripts/sc/tests/tc_d1_cer/test_s7.py::test_reenable_requires_actual_consumer_interface_input_and_command_bindings removes or substitutes a Consumer's actual interface, input, or command in its own receipt; the validator must observe the expected-red failure.

scripts/sc/tests/tc_d1_cer/test_s7.py::test_reenable_requires_actual_consumer_output_result_and_dependency_bindings removes or borrows a Consumer's actual output, result, or dependencies in its own receipt; the validator must observe the expected-red failure.

scripts/sc/tests/tc_d1_cer/test_s7.py::test_reenable_requires_real_candidate_route_invocation mutates the re-enable path so the Consumer does not call the Candidate Route; the validator must observe the expected-red failure.
